clue.text: As a booby prize it's wooden club

definitions.text: As a booby prize it's wooden
definitions.meaning: the wooden kind of this kitchen utensil is the mock trophy given to whoever comes last
an old wooden golf club with a lofted face went by the name of this utensil

explanation.definitionFit: The last-place award is a wooden kitchen utensil, and the same name was once given to a lofted wooden golf club.

clue.text: Felt so dumb, perhaps, avoiding motorway to show lack of confidence

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given are only one possible arrangement and must be rearranged
avoiding says the motorway letter is kept out of the phrase

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Someone who feels foolish and keeps off the motorway shows a lack of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes M from FELTSODUMB, and 'perhaps' rearranges the remaining FELTSODUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubting oneself is a want of confidence in one's own ability.

clue.text: Not starting cutting down, though in debt

indicators.note: not starting says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: mowing means cutting down grass or crops

explanation.surface: A man who hasn't begun mowing the lawn yet still owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still to be paid is owed, so a person who owes it is in debt.

clue.text: Nervous patient taking new Continental course?

parts.note: Euro- means European, of the Continent
a path is a course, a route

explanation.surface: An anxious patient takes a new route through Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suffering from a nervous disorder is a sufferer of the nerves, a patient with nerves.

clue.text: Bird providing picnic meal?

definitions.meaning: a large thrush that winters in Britain
food eaten out in a meadow, read as two words, food of the open country

explanation.definitionFit: The thrush's name splits into a meadow plus food, which is what a picnic out in the countryside amounts to.

clue.text: Plant removes obstacles from road going north

parts.note: frees means clears, removes obstacles from

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means the road's letters are read upwards

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's Great North Road, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A plant clears the blockages from a road heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's main north road; crosswords write it AI, and 'going north' turns it into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant grown from corms.

clue.text: Delightful vivacity about youth leader is uplifting

indicators.note: about says the vivacity word goes round the other letters

parts.note: elan means dash, vivacity

indicators.note: leader means the head of the word youth, its first letter
in a down clue uplifting means the little word is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young leader's lively spirit is truly inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reads as praise for the clue's surface, but in a down clue it turns the little word upwards; 'about' means going round, not concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium is the paradise of Greek myth, so something blissful and heavenly is delightful.

clue.text: Put up dirty sort of shirt that's hung out

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word is raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: lewd means dirty, obscene
T is the T-shirt

explanation.surface: Someone hangs up a filthy kind of shirt to dry outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang out somewhere informally is to live or stay there, an old sense of having resided.

clue.text: Recalling once a year without a fish

indicators.note: without says a letter a is removed from the yearly word

parts.note: annual means happening once a year
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Remembering an annual event that has no fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes an A from ANNUAL, leaving ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalling a decree or order means revoking or cancelling it.

clue.text: Girl I caught in time

indicators.note: in says the letters for I and caught go inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A girl says she was caught just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a girl's name.

clue.text: Floral necklace certainly makes one relaxed

parts.note: a lei is the Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck
surely means certainly, without doubt

explanation.surface: Wearing a garland of flowers is sure to make a person feel at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done unhurriedly and at ease is done in a relaxed way.

clue.text: Rotten nuisance, having such an attack of lassitude

annotationWithheld.why: Rotten nuisance, having such an attack of lassitude (5): the anagram of NUISANCE leaves S, A, C beyond ENNUI, and no clue word plainly supplies or removes them
annotationWithheld.clue: Rotten nuisance, having such an attack of lassitude

clue.text: Scoundrel has to leave hiding

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible fellow, a rogue
to go is to leave, depart

explanation.surface: A villain has to get out of his hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'lie doggo' is old British slang for staying hidden and keeping quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying low out of sight is the idiomatic sense, as in the phrase about lying still and concealed.

clue.text: Trace a bright spark

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, the merest hint of something
the Latin source word means a spark, a flash of light

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace is the English sense, while the Latin original names a spark or glimmer.

clue.text: Raised little money. ., unfortunately, back in city

parts.note: up means raised, lifted
p is the abbreviation for penny, a small coin

indicators.note: back says the word for unfortunately is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: alas is a cry meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Someone sadly lifted a small sum, then returned it in town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fundraiser; 'back' instead turns the sigh of regret round, and 'in' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a university city in Sweden, an example of a city.

clue.text: Ragged gamin taking part in sort of game

indicators.note: ragged means tattered, so the letters are torn apart and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A scruffy street urchin joins in some kind of game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragged' rearranges GAMIN plus PART. 'game' here means wild birds shot for sport, not a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse shot for sport, so it is a kind of game bird.

clue.text: Having a quick one — bitter?

definitions.meaning: taking a nip, a small quick drink of spirits
biting cold, as in a sharp frost

explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small drink, and a nipping wind is a bitterly cold one.

clue.text: Down-to-earth sort of joke

definitions.meaning: a prank played on someone, rather than a told joke

explanation.definitionFit: A sensible person is realistic and level-headed, and a prank is a joke carried out rather than spoken.

clue.text: Big-head's fame

parts.note: great means big
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: The fame of a conceited person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big-head' looks like one word for a show-off, but it splits: big gives the first part and head gives a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence and distinction are fame, the quality of being renowned.

clue.text: Feature on drink in public discussion

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, the facial feature follows the drink

parts.note: tea is the British everyday drink
the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature about drinking in a public debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal lecture and debate session on a public issue, typically at a university.

clue.text: Harassed, it's clear, and influenced

parts.note: nett means clear, as in clear profit after deductions
led means influenced, guided

explanation.surface: Someone was harassed, plainly, and swayed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritated and provoked is being harassed, as if stung.

clue.text: Bright little spot in naughty Naples about midnight

indicators.note: about says the shuffled city letters go round the middle letter
naughty suggests the city's letters misbehaving and getting out of order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
the middle letter of the word night is G

explanation.surface: A glittering spot in the wicked Italian city around twelve at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges NAPLES into SPANLE; 'about' puts it round G, the middle of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin, a small glittering ornament, is exactly a bright little spot.

clue.text: Behaves harshly towards boy from another union

definitions.meaning: treads on someone, treats them with contempt
a spouse's son from a previous marriage

explanation.definitionFit: Treading on someone is treating them harshly, and a spouse's son from an earlier marriage is a son by marriage only.

clue.text: Smash to get point — or a foot-fault?

parts.note: to hammer is to smash, pound
taken as written
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tennis player smashes to win the point, unless it is a foot fault.
explanation.walkthrough: A foot-fault is a tennis infringement, but here it means a deformity of a toe that is bent down at the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe that is permanently bent is a physical defect of the foot, a fault in it.

clue.text: Herculean effort finally halted its capital growth

definitions.text: Herculean effort finally halted its capital growth

parts.words: Herculean effort finally halted its capital growth
parts.note: one of the labours of Hercules killed a monster whose heads, capitals, kept growing back

explanation.surface: A huge final effort put a stop to the capital's economic growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital growth' reads as finance, but capital means heads: the many-headed serpent grew two for each one cut off until Hercules stopped it.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-headed serpent of Lerna sprouted new heads until Hercules cauterised the stumps.

clue.text: Celebrate former tax being cut

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: being cut says the tax word loses its last letter

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax for passage

explanation.surface: Celebrate the fact that an old tax is being reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise highly is to celebrate in words.

clue.text: Followed pronouncement in pamphlet

indicators.note: pronouncement says the word is to be heard spoken, not written

parts.note: tracked means followed, trailed

explanation.surface: Someone followed a statement printed in a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short religious or political leaflet, a kind of pamphlet.

clue.text: A fool's change of heart, becoming mature

indicators.note: change of heart says the middle letter of the word for fool is swapped for another

parts.note: a dolt is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool changes his mind and grows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the O at the centre of DOLT for U.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fully grown up is being mature.

clue.text: Take any number under ten — understand?

definitions.meaning: the slang question 'get it?', with dig meaning understand

explanation.definitionFit: A single figure is one of 0 to 9, and 'dig it?' is slang for 'do you understand?'.

clue.text: One you can no longer influence at home in Oxford

definitions.text: One you can no longer influence
definitions.meaning: a cause or person beyond saving, a hopeless case
Matthew Arnold called Oxford the home of hopeless causes

explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless cause cannot be won, and Arnold famously described Oxford as the home of such causes.

clue.text: Girl treated Daniel like a worm

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: treated as in processed, so the man's name is worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A girl has dealt with Daniel as if he were a worm.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelids are segmented worms such as earthworms, so the adjective means worm-like.

clue.text: Not a memorable meal for 'Tennyson's consumers

definitions.text: Not a memorable meal for 'Tennyson's consumers

parts.words: Not a memorable meal for 'Tennyson's consumers
parts.note: in Tennyson's poem the eaters of a certain fruit fall into dreamy forgetfulness, so the meal makes them forget everything

explanation.surface: A forgettable dinner for the people who read Tennyson.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's Lotos-Eaters ate the fruit and forgot their homes, so it was a meal that wiped memory.
